terms.gloss: threefold, triple, in three layers or lines
terms.comment: The everyday word for what is made of three parts or layers: Caesar’s battle line in three ranks, Horace’s triple bronze. Ablative triplicī.
Of amount, three times as much; triplō plūs, three times as many, is Plautus’s (Truc. 1.1.70; Lewis & Short). See double for duplex and duplus.

phrases.english: Let’s tie a triple knot so it won’t come undone.

phrases.latin: illī rōbur et aes triplex circā pectus erat
phrases.english: he had oak and triple bronze about his heart

phrases.latin: ipse interim in colle mediō triplicem aciem īnstrūxit legiōnum quattuor veterānārum
phrases.english: meanwhile he himself drew up the four veteran legions in a triple line halfway up the hill

sources: Lewis & Short: triplex · Lewis & Short: triplus
